members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: post_writer was started via tg.start_soon() with no readiness handshake, so a caller could proceed (yield the session / send the first message) before post_writer's write_stream_reader was actually being iterated — a startup race that could drop the first message or hang. Both PRs fix it the same way: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None]` parameter to post_writer and call `task_status.started(None)` immediately after entering the stream context manager, requiring callers to use `tg.start()` instead of `start_soon()`.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: post_writer was started via tg.start_soon() with no readiness handshake, so a caller could proceed (yield the session / send the first message) before post_writer's write_stream_reader was actually being iterated — a startup race that could drop the first message or hang. Both PRs fix it the same way: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None]` parameter to post_writer and call `task_status.started(None)` immediately after entering the stream context manager, requiring callers to use `tg.start()` instead of `start_soon()`.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs patch the exact same `if isinstance(data_value, str) and ...` guard in pre_parse_json to stop corrupting string values, but #2032's fix is strictly broader: its `_should_pre_parse_json`/`_SIMPLE_TYPES` check skips pre-parsing for any union composed only of str/int/float/bool/None (covering `str | int`, `str | bool`, multi-member unions, and `str | None`), while #3056's `_is_optional_str` only special-cases the single `str | None` / `Optional[str]` shape and leaves e.g. `str | int` unions still subject to corruption. #2032 also lands as one helper function versus #3056's two (`_unwrap_annotated` + `_is_optional_str`) for a narrower case. members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: RequestResponder.cancel() incorrectly sent an ad-hoc error response when a request was cancelled instead of following the spec-correct cancellation flow. #2493 branches from session.py@243eef5ae6 and simply deletes the 'send an error response to indicate cancellation' code from cancel(), and updates the matching comment/log in server.py's _handle_request to reflect that no response should ever be sent for a cancelled request. #2514 branches from the same session.py@243eef5ae6 base and touches the same cancel() method, but instead of just deleting the error-response code it imports CancelledNotificationParams and adds logic to emit a proper notifications/cancelled message for caller-initiated/timeout cancellations, which is what the MCP spec actually requires the cancelling party to send. Both PRs rewrite the same hunk of cancel() from the same base commit and directly conflict.
